key_terms.meaning: On-chip 8051 registers from 80H to FFH that control ports, timers, serial port and interrupts.
16-bit register holding the address of the next instruction byte to fetch.
16-bit data pointer formed by DPH and DPL, used to address external or data memory.
Program Status Word at 0D0H holding carry, auxiliary carry, register-bank select, overflow, parity and user flag.
One of four groups of eight registers R0 to R7, selected by RS1:RS0 in PSW.
Memory organisation with separate program and data memories and buses.
PIC16F877A fetches the next instruction while executing the current one, so most instructions take one cycle after the first.
PIC data memory split into banks selected by RP1:RP0 and IRP.
Two STATUS bits that select the active data memory bank in PIC.
PIC STATUS bit used as the bank-select bit for indirect addressing.
PIC reset vector; execution starts here after reset.
PIC interrupt vector; the interrupt service routine starts here.
Seven operating modes: User, FIQ, IRQ, Supervisor, Abort, Undefined and System.
Extra registers swapped in for R13, R14 and SPSR in each ARM mode, giving fast context.
ARM7 fetch, decode and execute stages; PC reads as current address plus 8.
Top four bits of a 32-bit ARM instruction that make it execute only if CPSR flags match.
Suffix on an ARM data-processing instruction that sets CPSR condition flags.
ARM state using 16-bit Thumb instructions; selected by the T bit in CPSR.
Rule that computes an operand's effective address from registers, constants and index.
Address plan assigning code, data, stack, I/O and peripherals to fixed address ranges.

takeaways: 8051 control lives in special function registers, so a small set of SFR bits sets ports, timers and serial mode.
PIC16F877A starts at reset vector 0000H, jumps to 0004H for interrupts, and selects data banks with RP1:RP0 and IRP.
ARM7 hides work behind seven modes and banked registers, so a mode switch changes R13, R14 and SPSR quickly.
The three-stage ARM pipeline means the visible PC is current instruction address plus 8.
ARM instructions are 32-bit and Thumb 16-bit; the condition field and S suffix decide when an instruction runs and whether flags change.
An addressing mode finds the operand, while a memory map decides where code, data, stack and registers live.
Assembly language gives one machine instruction per line, which makes exact delays and flag control possible.
Raspberry Pi runs Linux and hides timing, while Arduino runs bare-metal firmware and hides electrical detail; choose by task.

glossary.def: A single-chip computer with CPU, memory and peripherals for control tasks.
A CPU on a chip that needs external memory and peripherals to form a system.
A memory design with separate program and data memories and buses.
A memory design where program and data share the same memory and bus.
A design style with a small, simple instruction set, load-store memory access and many registers.
A design style with complex, variable-length instructions that may do more work per instruction.
An on-chip register that controls a peripheral or holds its status.
The register that holds the address of the next instruction to fetch.
The register that points to the top of the stack.
A group of registers that can be swapped in for fast context switching.
A design that overlaps instruction stages so several instructions are in progress at once.
The fixed address where the CPU starts execution after reset.
The fixed address where an interrupt service routine starts.
A privileged or unprivileged operating state with its own banked registers.
The current program status register holding condition flags and mode bits.
A 16-bit instruction subset of the ARM architecture used for code density.
A flag test that decides whether an instruction executes.
The rule an instruction uses to find or compute its operand address.
The address plan that assigns code, data, stack and I/O to fixed ranges.
A program that translates assembly language into machine code.
A compiler that runs on one computer and produces code for another target.
A file that tells the linker where to place code and data sections in memory.
A hardware debug tool that controls and observes a running microcontroller.
A general-purpose input/output pin used for digital signals.
A serial communication peripheral that sends and receives asynchronous data.
A counter peripheral used for delays, time measurement and events.
